item.title: Exploring the Interplay of Entrepreneurial Emotion, Judgment, and Decision Making
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines how emotions influence entrepreneurial judgment and decision-making, particularly in community-based and localized ecosystems. While existing research has focused on positive emotions like passion and resilience, the issue seeks to explore understudied emotional domains such as despair, awe, humility, guilt, empathy, and regret that shape entrepreneurs' strategic choices, resilience, and ethical judgments.

The special issue welcomes interdisciplinary research on how diverse emotional experiences affect entrepreneurial cognition and behavior within small businesses, family firms, and social enterprises. It invites both quantitative approaches examining causal relationships and qualitative studies exploring contextualized experiences, alongside theoretical contributions offering new frameworks for understanding emotions in entrepreneurship.

Insights from this research aim to inform policy-making, entrepreneurial education, and support structures by revealing how emotional dynamics drive sustainable business practices, ethical decision-making, and community engagement in localized entrepreneurial ecosystems.

Appel publié par Journal of Enterprising Communities: People and Places in the Global Economy. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Entrepreneurial Decision Making in Digital and Algorithm-Driven Environments
  • Emotion Regulation in Crisis and Disruptive Contexts
  • Impact of Virtual and Augmented Reality on Entrepreneurial Emotion and Judgment
  • Cross-Generational Differences in Emotional Decision-Making in Family Businesses
  • Entrepreneurial Emotion and Decision-Making in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations
  • Emotional Labor and Well-being in Serial Entrepreneurship
  • Role of Synthetic and AI-Generated Emotions in Entrepreneurial Decision-Making
  • Humility in Entrepreneurial Learning and Adaptation
  • Empathy and Ethical Decision-Making in Social Entrepreneurship
  • Entrepreneurial Despair: Causes and Consequences
  • Pride and Self-Efficacy in Sustained Entrepreneurial Motivation
  • Envy in Competitive Strategy and Innovation
  • Entrepreneurial emotional dilemma: social or conventional/traditional entrepreneurship?
  • Inner accomplishment and entrepreneurship

  • December 31, 2026: Closing date for manuscript submissions

item.title: Social Good under Transformation: New Contexts for Social Entrepreneurship
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks to advance understanding of social entrepreneurship in rapidly transforming global contexts. We invite submissions that explore how social enterprises are adapting to new economic, technological, and social environments while maintaining their commitment to social and environmental impact.

Appel publié par European Management Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Social entrepreneurship in evolving markets and contexts
  • Impact measurement and evaluation of social enterprises
  • Hybrid business models combining social and commercial goals
  • Digital transformation and social entrepreneurship
  • Policy and regulatory frameworks for social enterprises
  • Stakeholder engagement and partnerships in social entrepreneurship
  • Scaling social impact
  • Environmental sustainability and social entrepreneurship

Timeline

  • October 31, 2026: Full paper submission deadline
